prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map reveals a multi-level construction scene where the camera wearer stands on an elevated platform beside a plastered wall and overhang within arm's reach (0.3–1.0 m in the upper-left of frames 1–2 and filling the left and top of frame 3), looking down at a lower bamboo scaffolding level (roughly 1.5–2.5 m below) and the ground floor (3–4 m below). In frames 1 and 2, a worker in a plaid shirt and head wrap stands on the ground/lower level about 2.5–3.5 m below and in front of the wearer, facing toward a cement bucket and round mortar pans within his arm's reach (0.3–0.5 m to his right) while looking down away from the wearer, and the wearer's own trowel and hand appear at the bottom edge of frame 1 within 0.5 m. Across frames 1 to 3, the wearer turns and tilts their head upward and to the left so the nearby wall corner (0.3–0.8 m) and brick wall behind it (1.5–2.5 m) occlude the lower scaffolding, before looking back down in frames 4 and 5 as the lower worker shifts toward the upper-left of the frame (roughly 2–3 m below, partially occluded by the upper ledge in frame 4 and cropped by the top-left border in frame 5) while two foreground mortar pans sit on the scaffolding within 0.5–1.2 m at the bottom and right. The depth map clearly separates the vertical layers—distinguishing the foreground mortar pans, intermediate bamboo poles, and distant ground better than the cluttered, shadowed RGB image—though it is unreliable where thin bamboo gaps blur together and in frame 5 where the ground behind the scaffolding becomes uniformly black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of entities across the five frames of the multi-level construction site, localizing the lower worker ('person') at roughly 2.5–3.5 m below the camera wearer in frame 1 and again in the upper-left of frame 5 at about 2–2.5 m distance as the camera pans down and right. In frame 1, it also segments the camera wearer's trowel and hand at the bottom-center edge (within 0.4–0.6 m, arm's reach of the wearer) and in frame 5 it segments the round mortar pan resting on the bamboo scaffolding to the right (about 1.0–1.5 m below the wearer and roughly 1.0–1.5 m to the right of the worker). While the RGB context shows the worker facing forward/right toward his buckets and looking down away from the elevated camera wearer, and shows a second person's pink-sleeved arm partially occluded under the upper ledge in frame 4 about 2.5 m below, the segmentation masks only provide 2D silhouettes that shift from center-left (frame 1) to absent (frames 2–4, including when the wall occludes the scene in frame 3) to upper-left and center-right (frame 5). Compared to the busy RGB image, the masks sharply isolate the silhouette of the worker and the circular pan from the crosshatched bamboo poles and shadows, but the map is highly unreliable: it misses the worker entirely in frames 2 and 4, misses the large foreground pan at the bottom of frames 4 and 5 (within 0.5–0.8 m of the wearer), and mislabels the wearer's trowel/hand in frame 1 as 'cat' and the mortar pan in frame 5 as 'toilet'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map extracts 2D yellow body skeletons for the worker located about 2.5–3.5 m below the camera wearer in frames 1 and 2, while remained completely blank in frames 3, 4, and 5 and detecting no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In frames 1 and 2, the keypoints trace the worker's head, torso, and outstretched arms from an overhead angle, showing his torso oriented toward the lower-right of the image with both arms extended 0.3–0.5 m forward to grasp and tilt the cement bucket over the round pan within his arm's reach, while his head is angled downward away from the camera wearer. From frame 1 to frame 2, as the camera tilts slightly upward and left toward the nearby wall, the detected skeleton shifts toward the bottom-left corner of the frame and elongates as the worker leans further over the pan, with his lower legs occluded and cropped at the bottom edge of frame 2. This skeletal wireframe clarifies the overhead orientation of the worker's shoulders, elbows, and head through the cluttered bamboo shadows better than the RGB image alone, but it is unreliable under extreme top-down foreshortening—compressing the torso into a box-like shape, failing to detect the worker's hands or the camera wearer's own hand within 0.5 m in frame 1, and failing to detect the worker in frames 4 and 5 when he is partially occluded or seen from behind and above.
